exercises.title: The vowel you barely say
exercises.body: Lesson 40 showed you how much 𐑩 there is to read. Writing it is harder, because English keeps a proper-looking vowel on the page — the o of problem, the a of sofa — and your hand wants to copy it. Do not. If the syllable is unstressed and you barely say it, it is 𐑩.

exercises.title: Say it aloud, slowly
exercises.body: The trick is to say the word at normal speed, not spelling speed. Say problem carefully and you might invent an o that is not there; say it as you would to a friend and you hear 𐑐𐑮𐑪𐑚𐑤𐑩𐑥. Little is 𐑤𐑦𐑑𐑩𐑤, opened is 𐑴𐑐𐑩𐑯𐑛.

exercises.title: 𐑩 or 𐑼?
exercises.body: One question decides between them: is there an r in the sound? The mumbled ending of better, summer and paper is not 𐑩 but 𐑼 — the array vowel from the last lesson. 𐑚𐑧𐑑𐑼, 𐑕𐑳𐑥𐑼, 𐑐𐑱𐑐𐑼. Keep 𐑩 for the mumble with no r in it.
